title: Raspberry Pi 4 Model B
description: Raspberry Pi 4B review, including the hardware specs of this new single board computer, and a demo running the latest version of Raspbian. With thanks to the Raspberry Pi Foundation for supplying the board featured in this video.  You can learn more about the Raspberry Pi 4B on the Raspberry Pi Foundation website here: https://www.raspberrypi.org/products/raspberry-pi-4-model-b/  You can see some of my performance tests of the Raspberry Pi 4B in this video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kbn_6ixtIpA  The Pi 4B can be purchased from many suppliers. Some of my favourites include DFRobot (see: https://www.dfrobot.com/product-1873.html ), Pimoroni (see: https://shop.pimoroni.com/products/raspberry-pi-4?variant=29157087445075 ) and Adafruit (see: https://www.adafruit.com/product/4296 ). I will add Amazon links here when available.  You can find a playlist of my previous videos featuring the Raspberry Pi 3 B+ and 3A+ here: https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PL2m2YvnrOYxIABPXD2YY-ilcy_quyyEbT  And here is my video introducing the Python programming language: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Crsp_He70no  More videos on single board computers and other computing topics can be found on the ExplainingComputers channel: https://www.youtube.com/user/explainingcomputers/videos  You may also like my other channel, ExplainingTheFuture, at: https://www.youtube.com/user/explainingthefuture/videos  #RaspberryPi4i #Pi4B #ExplainingComputers

At that in a lot more depth obviously a bit later in the video and in addition. That we have a Raspberry Pi mouse and we have a new Raspberry Pi USB-C power supply. Yes,. The Raspberry Pi 4B uses a USB-C power supply. That's one of our first changes to the Pi. And beneath here, this slips out, I'm sure, it does something like this. Come out, come. Out. There we are. Under here, we've got a Raspberry Pi keyboard and hub. That looks. Rather nice and also down here we've got some connection leads so lots of. Exciting things in this desktop kit but I'm sure initially at least the thing. You're most interested in is the Raspberry Pi 4B itself which will be. Inside this case which I think just clicks apart there it is there is the. Raspberry Pi 4B so let's take a closer look at this new Pi. So, I've now put the accessories safely to one side so we can take a closer look at the. Star of our show, the brand new Raspberry Pi 4B. And the second surprise to reveal here is that you can buy a Raspberry Pi 4B in one. Of three different versions, because you can buy a Raspberry Pi 4B with either 1, 2 or. 4 gigabytes of RAM. And to give you the prices, the 1GB Raspberry Pi 4B costs £33 or $35, the 2GB Raspberry. Pi 4B costs £43 or $45, and the 4GB Raspberry Pi 4B costs £53 or $55. So you can make your choice in terms of price, in terms of how much RAM you have on your. Raspberry Pi 4B. Now as you probably noticed already, things have changed a bit on the top of the Pi. Components are slightly different in some cases so let's compare this to the. Previous Raspberry Pi 3B Plus and there we are the new Pi is now sitting next to. Its older comrade and straight away you can see that they've switched over the. Position of the USB ports and the ethernet socket which is now a mirror of. The previous Pi and we can see we've got our USB-C power connector here compared. To the micro USB power connector on previous Pis and other changes down here. Which I'll get to in a second. And what all this means is whilst the Pi is compatible with previous. Models, the Raspberry Pi 4B, it's got the same form factor, it won't go in the same cases. We need new cases for the Raspberry Pi 4B. So let's take a bit of a closer look at the specs. Of this board. And the Raspberry Pi 4B is based on a Broadcom BCM2711 system on a chip with a 64-bit. Quad-core ARM Cortex-A72 CPU running at 1.5GHz. As just noted this is paired with. One two or four gigabytes of RAM that's a low power DDR4 RAM and the board also. Has good wireless connectivity specifically it's got dual band 802.1.1b. GNNAC Wi-Fi and Bluetooth 5.0 and as you've probably noticed if you're into. Your Pis we still have the camera connector and display connector on the. Top of the board in exactly the same positions they were previously, the MIPI. CSI and DSI connectors, but just as we found them on previous Pis. If we turn to. The first short edge things get very exciting because for the first time on a. Pi we've got gigabit Ethernet and then our four Type-A USB ports as you can see. Here, two of them as you've probably noticed already are USB 3. So yes we've. Got two USB 3 ports and gigabit Ethernet on a Pi. So if for example you want to. Use a Pi to build a NAS that's very good news indeed. Rotating around to the first. Long edge we find a familiar 3.5 millimeter jack for audio and composite. Video output and then at the other end of this edge we have our USB-C power. Connector and the Raspberry Pi 4B requires 5 volts at at least 3 amps. Which can be delivered either through this USB-C connector or by GPO or using a. Power of an Ethernet hat. And then in the middle of those connectors we find two,. Count them two, micro HDMI connectors. Yes the full-size HDMI connector has gone to. Be replaced with these two micro HDMI ports. And so if you're wondering why. There were two leads in the desktop kit, this is why. We now have dual display. Support on a Raspberry Pi. And these micro HDMI connectors support resolutions. Up to 4K. And in this context it's also worth noting that the Raspberry Pi 4B offers hardware. Decoding of both 1080p and 4K video at up to 60 frames a second. Turning to the second short edge. We find that nothing has changed. We still have a display connector where it was on previous Pis. And similarly if we turn to the second long edge we find no changes again. We've got our familiar. 40 pin Raspberry Pi GPIO connector and also the 4 pin power over Ethernet or PoE connector. First introduced on the Raspberry Pi 3B+. If we move back to the top of the board and I'll just. Show you underneath because of course we do have underneath the micro SD card slot which obviously. We're putting a card in very soon to boot up the Pi but other than that nothing of great excitement. Underneath. And so there we are, that is the spec of our new Raspberry Pi 4B. And. Just to give you a summary, this is a Raspberry Pi with one, two or four. Gigabytes of RAM, two USB 3 ports, gigabit Ethernet, USB-C power and dual 4k. Output. And so I think by anybody's measure this is a very significant. Upgrade to the Raspberry Pi. So let's take a brief look at the Raspberry Pi 4B accessories and the first of these is the power. Supply which we have here already removed it from its little box and this provides the 5 volts 3. Amps necessary to run the Raspberry Pi 4B with its USB-C connector on the end and the thing we. Like about this it's got a very very long lead which is great to see on a power supply so often. I have to put an extension lead on a power supply for a single board computer. I won't have to do that for this one. It's got a nice long lead and. Talking of leads. These are the two HDMI leads that came in the box. They've got the micro HDMI well then to go into the PI and full-size. HDMI at the other to go into a monitor or a recorder or whatever else you're putting them into and. Here again is the case which we saw earlier the PI came in the case a standard Raspberry Pi case. But obviously we designed to take the Raspberry Pi 4B, different cutouts to previous cases, and. Very easy to put the Pi in here. You just literally drop it in. Like this, and then you drop the cover. On the top and it all. Clips down if I can get it right. There we are, and the Pi is now. Easily in the case, and you can just put your micro SD card in the back, and that just goes in there. I think like that, so the Pi is all ready for action. But of course to use the Pi it has to have a keyboard and a mouse and as we saw in the Raspberry Pi kit. There was the Raspberry Pi Mouse. This is released earlier, I think in. 2019. Need to bring in a Stanley of a knife to let us in there. Never seen a Raspberry Pi mouse before in the in the flesh or the plastic although it is it's got a red. Scroller that's rather nicer looking mouse and. And finally we have the Raspberry Pi keyboard and hub which we will open up by the magic of filmmaking. And it's actually a rather nice keyboard. It's very similar to the keyboard I use a lot of the time. Nice soft keys, very good if you've got arthritis or RSI, things like that. Good spacebar action. And as you can see here, it has got the hub at the back. It's got three USB Type-A ports there. There and it plugs into the Pi using this red lead which goes in like that into micro USB. That will go into the Pi and it gives you the extra USB port to have a hub at the back. So. There we are. It's now time to put all of this together and to boot up the Raspberry Pi 4 Model B. So here we are booting into Raspbian on the Raspberry Pi 4B and this is a new version of. Raspbian released concurrently with the Raspberry Pi 4B to support obviously its new hardware and. In fact what I'm running here is probably a pre-release because I've been supplied this. Before release day and I don't necessarily have everything here I don't think and if we look into. Programming stuff is there, internet. We don't have for example LibreOffice. Installed here, so this might not be final software. I don't know, so I don't. Want to judge it too much on that. And because of that I'm therefore not going. To do significant performance tests in this video. I will leave those to future. Videos. But it's interesting I think to look here we go to accessories and the. Task manager and you'll see that we've got our 3731 megabytes of RAM. There. This is a 4 gigabyte Raspberry Pi 4B. The other memory is being used by the. GPU here, we go to preferences and Pi configuration, you'll see my GPU is. Allocated 256 megabytes which we can do on a Pi with a 4 gigabytes of RAM. I've. Still got to get my head around the fact we can now buy Raspberry Pi with one, two. Or four gigabytes of RAM. And talking of the GPU will make you start to think. About graphical performance, let's just have a little bit look at that. Let's go. Into the Chromium web browser and here we are. We can clearly do normal web. Browsing very well indeed. I'll have to upgrade my SBC page here, won't I? Put the Raspberry Pi 4B. At the top of that, paste that. And if we go to, say, YouTube and play a sample clip, I know that's. What you all want to see me do. We'll just full screen that, and hopefully it'll catch up. There. We are. This will be playing in 1080p, I think. Yes, this is 1080p. And this looks pretty good. This is much better than we'd normally see on a Raspberry Pi, isn't it? This is rather good. Playback. And that's clearly a very good thing. Raspberry Pis have struggled a bit with media. Playback for a while now, and clearly with this latest upgrade, we aren't going to have that. Problem anymore. So that's very good to see. And I think for now I'm going to leave this,. Because I've got to come back and do all sorts of tests in future videos, tests of cooling and. Performance and all that type of thing. But the one thing I would say is that the desktop experience. Here is just very nice, it's very fluid. And the Raspberry Pi Foundation in their marketing for the. Raspberry Pi 4B suggested it has performance comparable to entry-level x86 systems, and I. Think that's a fair comparison to make. And that's not to suggest that a Raspberry Pi 4B is the same. As the average desktop PC, it obviously isn't. But if you want to do basic computing on a Raspberry. Pi 4B, things like web browsing, a bit of media playback, email, a bit of office work, that type. It's very much well up to that task. And I'm sure that's why they now sell the. Raspberry Pi 4B desktop kit as we were previously looking at. So there we are. This is Raspbian on the Raspberry Pi 4B. It's always great to see Raspbian running. Regardless, I think it's just a nice operating system to use and I'll be testing it out a lot more in future videos. The Raspberry Pi 4B is a very significant upgrade that will have a very large impact. On the SBC marketplace. Why? Well, because for a few years now, if you've wanted to buy a Pi-priced single-board computer,. You've had a trade-off to make. On the one hand, you could have bought a Raspberry Pi, a 3B, a 3B+, with fantastic software support,. Support for the GPU in the software, not least, and fantastic community support. Or you could. Have bought a competitor board with far worse software support, far worse community support,. But competitor boards have increasingly had features not found on the Pi. Things like. A USB 3 port, gigabit ethernet, more memory, and 4K output. And so now we've got on a Raspberry. Pi USB 3 port, gigabit ethernet, more memory, 4K output. There are far fewer reasons to. Buy a competitive board, and so the Raspberry Pi 4B could blow many of its competitors out. Of the market. I very much look forward to testing out the Raspberry Pi 4B in future videos, using it. In projects, running performance tests, probably doing a new cooling video, and I'd be very. Interested to hear what you think of the new Raspberry Pi 4B, what you plan to do with. Please let us all know down in the comments section. But now that's it for another video. If you enjoyed what you've seen here, please press that like button. If you haven't subscribed, please subscribe, and I hope to talk to you again very soon. Thank you.
